biography_references.documented_chronology: Babbage studied at Cambridge from 1810, established a London home in 1815, and lived at Dorset Street, Marylebone, from 1828 until his death in 1871.
Tompion lived at Ickwell Green, Bedfordshire, and is documented in London in 1671, establishing his Water Lane business. He supplied a Tower of London clock in 1674.

Bardeen worked in Pittsburgh in 1930-1933, then studied at Princeton and worked at Harvard, Minnesota, and the Naval Ordnance Laboratory in Washington. He joined Bell Laboratories in 1945 and the University of Illinois in 1951.
biography_references.source: Nobel Prize, John Bardeen biographical record

biography_references.documented_chronology: Dyson studied at Byam Shaw in 1965-1966 and the Royal College of Art in 1966-1970 before working at Rotork. The company biography also documents his work with the Singapore team at St James Power Station in 2022.

Benerito was born in New Orleans, studied at Newcomb, Bryn Mawr, Tulane, and Chicago, earning her doctorate in 1948. After teaching at Newcomb, she joined the USDA Southern Regional Research Center in 1953 and remained for over thirty years.

Simjian was born in Turkey in 1905 and fled via Beirut and Marseille after World War I. At fifteen he arrived in the United States and settled with relatives in New Haven; in 1928 he became director of photography at Yale medical school.

Gallo, a Connecticut native, spent thirty years at the NIH National Cancer Institute, heading its Laboratory of Tumor Cell Biology, before becoming director of the University of Maryland Institute of Human Virology in 1996.
biography_references.source: University of Maryland School of Medicine, Institute of Human Virology

biography_references.documented_chronology: Carver grew up in Missouri and attended schools in Missouri and Kansas, enrolled at Simpson College in 1890, and transferred to Iowa State in 1891. After his 1896 master's degree he joined Tuskegee Institute in Alabama, where he worked until 1943.
biography_references.source: U.S. National Park Service, Tuskegee Institute National Historic Site

biography_references.documented_chronology: Fuller was born in Milton, Massachusetts, and attended Harvard. In the late 1950s he became a Southern Illinois University professor and lived with his wife in a geodesic dome during residence there. In 1972 he took a Philadelphia consortium residency; his career included extensive international travel.
biography_references.source: Buckminster Fuller Institute, Estate of R. Buckminster Fuller biography

biography_references.documented_chronology: West graduated from Temple University in 1957. Following his Bell Laboratories career, he retired from Bell in 2001 and joined Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore as a research professor.
biography_references.source: Johns Hopkins University, Whiting School of Engineering

biography_references.documented_chronology: Von Ohain was born in Dessau, studied at Goettingen, and developed engines at Heinkel in Germany in 1936-1939. He moved to America in 1947 and subsequently worked at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio.
Ford left the family farm for work in Detroit in 1879, returned home in 1882, and moved with Clara to Detroit in 1891 to work for Edison Illuminating. He incorporated Ford Motor Company in 1903.

Hertz was born in Hamburg, studied in Dresden, Munich, and Berlin, and earned his Berlin doctorate in 1880. He moved to Kiel in 1883, held the Karlsruhe physics chair in 1885-1889, and moved to Bonn in 1889.
